purpose:
To consider the recommendations of the report in relation
to the allocation of Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) Funds for
2026.
content:
To consider the recommendations of the report in relation
to the allocation of Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) Funds for
2026.

It was RESOLVED that the Cabinet
APPROVED:
 

a)   
The recommendations
for the allocation of Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) funding,
in accordance with the CIL Spending Protocol, as set out in
Appendices A and B;
 

b)   
That the funding of
£75,000 previously allocated in 2024 towards Alton Tennis
Club Padel Court Plan be reallocated to their new canopy project to
allow all year round tennis as detailed in paragraph
5.5;
 

d)   
That any decision
to remove CIL allocations from ‘at risk’ projects as
detailed in paragraph 8.2 be delegated to the Executive Director of
Operations in consultation with the Portfolio Holder for Regulation
and Enforcement;
 
The Cabinet also NOTED:
 

e)       The proposed
allocation of strategic CIL received from the Land   East of Horndean
development for education purposes as detailed in paragraph 6.3
and;
 

f)        The progress
of all projects allocated CIL funding since 2021 (Appendix D), with
many completed providing significant benefits for local
communities.

 

Reasons for the
Decision

 
To present to the Cabinet the recommendations for the
allocation of Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) funding for the
2026 spending application process and to recommend the use of the
CIL funding in accordance with the CIL spending protocol for the
new school at Hazleton Farm.
 
Alternative Options Considered
 
Option 1: Do nothing – No
allocation of CIL funds 
 
This option was not recommended on the basis that there is
a great opportunity to fund and help deliver infrastructure
projects that are of high value to local communities, helping to
enrich lives. Doing so helps demonstrate that whilst not solving
all problems by any means, there is a worthwhile contribution from
development towards infrastructure provision.? To not do so would
be failing those the money would benefit.
 
Option 2: Allocate CIL funds 
 
This was the only option that enables the Council to assist
with the delivery of key infrastructure projects in the district
and helps to support local communities. As set out in the Protocol,
it is important the Council does so in line with
legislation.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the allocation of Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) funds for 2026, including reallocating funds for a tennis club project and delegating decisions on 'at risk' projects.

content:
To consider an update on work undertaken since the decision
of the Cabinet in February 2024 and recommendations in respect of
future work.

It was RESOLVED that Cabinet
NOTED:
 
The improvements made in simplifying
access to our Council services, the support that has been put in
place for those who need it, specifically the in-person face to
face support available, and that there is no longer the demand for
a virtual solution.
 
Reasons for the
Decision
 
To update the Cabinet on the progress made with
transferring the delivery of customer  services, following the Cabinet decision on 22
February 2024 detailing the transformation plans for delivering
customer services to agree the future provision.
 
Alternative Options Considered
 
·      
The key aim of
transformation was to improve the digital offering, making it
simpler to access our services online in order to achieve
significant channel shift, with help available via the telephone
for those customers who needed it.
 
·      
For some customers
digital is not a viable option and therefore the Council needed to
ensure that services were accessible to all customers.
 
·      
Based on the
anticipated need at that time, it was proposed that a live link
solution should be developed to allow virtual face to face meetings
to take place from locations across the district.

It was RESOLVED that the Cabinet
APPROVED:
 
Option 2 of the report - The procurement
of Unit 4 ERPx through the G-Cloud
14
 
Reasons for the Decision
 
To seek authority from the Cabinet to procure a Financial
Management System to be used by East Hampshire District
Council.
 
Alternative Options Considered
 
Option 1 –
Extend existing contract and re-procure in 2027.
 
Whist initially appearing to be the simplest way to
proceed, this is not the best
value for money and simply delays the decision.
 




Extend to 2027



£
94,000




New contract Yr 1 (27/28)



£
215,000




New contract Yr 2 (28/29)



£
215,000




Total



£
524,000





 
Option 2 – Procure through G-Cloud
14 and award to existing provider.
 
A
new procurement before the end of the G-Cloud 14 framework allows
access to the lower prices in this schedule.
 




New contract Yr 1 (26/27)



£
140,000




New contract Yr 2 (27/28)



£
140,000




New contract Yr 3 (28/29)



£
140,000




Total



£
420,000




Remaining with the existing supplier also
allows EHDC to continue to build on the investment it has made thus
far and will avoid additional implementation costs associated with
a change of provider.
Option 3 – Procure an alternative
solution:
Under LGR, EHDC is scheduled to be
abolished on 31st March 2028. Any robust competitive procurement
and implementation is a 18 month project. This would therefore lead
to a go live date at best somewhen in late 2027.
Changing to a new provider would also
incur direct implementation costs of approximately
£250,000.
 
Due to the timescales and large
additional cost, this is not a viable option.

purpose:

content:
To consider the recommendations of the report, in relation
to Community Services Funding.

It was RESOLVED that the
Cabinet:
 

a)       Revoked the decision
made on 12 March 2026 to enter into a Service Level Agreement with
Community First East Hampshire for 2026/27
 

b)       Approved the
reallocation of the £60,000 budget provision to support an
alternative delivery model to progress the Councils work on
ABCD. 
 

c)       Delegated authority
to the Executive Director of Communities, in consultation with the
Portfolio Holder for Community Development and Engagement and the
Section 151 Officer, to determine and implement the most
appropriate use of the funding to support community capacity
building and community resilience.

 

Reasons for the
Decision

 
To seek the Cabinet approval to revise the funding
arrangements approved for Community First East Hampshire and
reallocate the funding to support the Council's Asset Based
Community Development programme.
 
Alternative Options Considered
 
Option A - Continue funding Community
First
This option would maintain continuity of the existing
arrangement and retain
access to specialist VCSE support services. However,
officers do not consider
that continuation of the current funding arrangement
provides the strongest
alignment with the Council's strategic priorities or the
best use of the available
funding.
 
Option B - Withdraw
funding with no replacement
This option would reduce expenditure but would remove
support currently available to communities and voluntary
organisations. Officers do not consider this option consistent with
the Council's commitment to supporting thriving
communities.
 
Option C - Reallocate funding to
community capacity building activity (Preferred Option)
This option would enable the Council to invest
directly in activity that supports its ABCD programme and wider transformation agenda. Funding
could be used flexibly to support community asset mapping,
community leadership, community builder approaches and other
community capacity building activity. Where specialist support is
required, the Council could commission external organisations, including Community First, to
provide specific pieces of work.
 
Officers considered this option provided the
greatest alignment with the Council's strategic priorities and
would offer the best opportunity to test new approaches to
supporting communities ahead of Local Government
Reorganisation.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to reallocate funding for Community Services to support the Council's Asset Based Community Development programme.

Reasons for the Decision:
To consider, in the Council's capacity as a

company's Business Plan for 2026/27 (Appendix A), as required by

To receive and consider the recommendations of the

It was RESOLVED that the Shareholders Sub
Committee:
 
a)             
Authorised East
Hampshire Norse Ltd. (as a Reserved Matter under Schedule 1 of the
Shareholders’ Agreement), to vary the Service Agreement to
include a Food Waste Collection Service to commence in October
2026. The service to be provided on the basis set out in exempt
appendix A.
 
b)             
Authorised East
Hampshire Norse Ltd (as a Reserved Matter under Article 6.3(l) and
(m) of the Articles of Association and Schedule 1 paragraphs (l),
(m) and (n) of the Shareholders’ Agreement), to  enter into the lease of Unit 78 Woolmer Way,
Bordon, on the principal commercial terms set out in exempt
appendix B  and exempt appendix
C.
 
c)             
Noted: the
cost-recovery framework, funding position and affordability outlook
at section 5. and in exempt appendix A.

 
 
Reasons for the Decision:
 
To consider, in the Council's capacity as shareholder in
East Hampshire Norse Limited (EHN), two interlinked Reserved Matter
decisions arising from the parallel papers submitted by EHN's
Partnership Director: the mobilisation and delivery of the Food
Waste Collection Service from October 2026, and the entry by EHN
into a lease of Unit 78 Woolmer Way, Bordon to serve as the
operational depot for that service.
 
Alternative Options
Considered:
 
The Shareholder Sub Committee was asked to make two linked
decisions. The food waste mobilisation requires additional
facilities to operate the expanded service. Refusal of either
recommendation jeopardises the delivery of the new
service.
 
The Government's Simpler Recycling requirements impose a
statutory duty on
waste collection authorities in England to provide weekly
household food waste collections. As such, EHDC must arrange for
the delivery of this service or risk fines and government
intervention. EHDC has engaged with EHN to deliver the service as a
variation to the Council's existing Service Agreement.
topline: The Shareholders Sub Committee has decided to authorize East Hampshire Norse Ltd. to implement a Food Waste Collection Service and enter into a lease agreement for Unit 78 Woolmer Way, Bordon.

platform and citizen services applications. Key services

complaints handling, and the IT  helpdesk would be severely disrupted. A replacement
procurement and  implementation exercise
would take an estimated 12–18 months.

purpose:
To consider and approve the recommendation of the
report.
content:
To consider and approve the recommendation of the
report.

It was RESOLVED that Cabinet:
 
a.       Approved the
realignment of Local Plan activity, transitioning from progression
of a local planning authority-based East Hampshire Local Plan under
the legacy planning system to engaging with the new planning system
and preparation for future unitary?wide plan?making, and
 
b.       Noted
that: 
 
To exercise its duties regarding plan making,
the Council will have to engage with the new planning system (which
will be the subject of a future report to Cabinet along with a
timetable), and;
 
work undertaken to date will be retained and
adapted to inform:
 
• future unitary Local
Plans;
• neighbourhood planning
support;
• development management
decision?making; and
• monitoring of housing supply and
delivery during the transition period.
 
Reasons for the Decision 
 
This paper is submitted to Cabinet to seek approval to
realign the Local Plan timetable and plan-making activity to engage
with the new planning system1, and to start to strategically
prepare for future plan making as part of the forthcoming unitary
authorities.
 
The report explains why, following a series of Government
changes culminating in the announcement of new unitary geographies
on 25 March 2026, the continued progression of a local planning
authority-based East Hampshire Local Plan presents significant
legal, financial, governance and practical risks, and why a
transition to the new planning system represents the most
responsible and proportionate course of action. In due course, this
would include preparation for unitary-wide plan-making with other
relevant planning authorities.
 
Alternative Options
Considered:
 
Option 1:
Continue progressing the East Hampshire
Local Plan under the
legacy system(not recommended)
 
This option would involve continuing towards Regulation 19
submission by 31
December 2026. While this would maintain continuity with
previous work, it carries significant risks, including:
 

•       
substantial further
financial expenditure with an increased risk of
abortive costs;

·      
unresolved strategic
evidence issues, including transport and water
supply constraints;

•       
a high likelihood that
the plan would not be adopted before vesting day;

•       
legal, procedural and
political uncertainty arising from the division of
East Hampshire between two successor authorities;
and

•       
the risk that the plan
would be rendered out of date by the revised
NPPF and emerging strategic planning
arrangements.
 
For these reasons, this option is not considered
to represent a proportionate or responsible course of
action.
 
 
Option 2:
Pause plan?making
activity entirely (not recommended)
 
This option would reduce short?term
expenditure but would risk losing momentum, weakening the
Council’s evidence base, and undermining support for
neighbourhood planning and development
management decision?making during the transition period. This
option is inconsistent with national planning policy, which
confirms that the planning system should be genuinely plan-led
(paragraph 15, NPPF). At a meeting on 27 April 2026 with appointed
Local Plan Counsel, this option was advised against.
 
Option 3:
Engage with the new planning system whilst preparing for
plan?making of unitary?wide Local Plans (recommended)
 
This option involves transitioning to the progression of a
district-based Local Plan under the new plan-making system. As time
moves forward, discussions and jointworking with other local planning authorities
and stakeholders relevant to the emerging Mid Hants and South East
Unitary Authorities would enable this plan to be better aligned
with emerging priorities for the respective areas.
 
This option:
 

•       
avoids potentially
abortive expenditure;

•       
allows existing
evidence and engagement to be retained and adapted;

•       
reduces legal,
financial and governance risk;

•       
supports effective
planning decision?making
during the transition period; and

•       
places successor
authorities in a stronger position to prepare coherent, strategic
Local Plans.
 
Officers therefore
recommended Option 3 as the most proportionate, defensible and
future?focused approach.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to realign Local Plan activity in East Hampshire to transition to the new planning system and prepare for future unitary-wide plan-making.

Local Government (MHCLG) for the administration and delivery of the
Local Authority Housing Fund – fourth funding round

content:

relation to the PAS Planning Committee Review.

It was RESOLVED that Cabinet:

a.    
Received the PAS
Planning Committee Review report (Appendix A) and recommend that
Full Council notes the positive commentary and areas for
improvement identified.

b.   
Agreed the Action
Plan (Appendix B) to address the recommendations of the review,
noting the actions already implemented.

c.    
Agreed that
preparatory work commence on a revised Scheme of Delegation and
associated constitutional changes to align with the draft national
scheme of delegation, with final adoption to follow once the
Regulations are made.

d.   
Agreed that
progress on the Action Plan be reviewed after 12
months.

Reasons for the Decision
This report presents
the findings from the Planning Advisory Service (PAS) Planning
Committee Review (February 2026) and proposes next steps to
strengthen decision?making, governance and
performance of the Planning Committee.
The review was
commissioned proactively in response to the potential designation
risk (Section 62B, Town and Country Planning Act 1990) linked to
the quality of decision?making on Major
applications, with the intention of taking early action to improve
robustness and resilience. The review provides an independent
assessment of the operation, effectiveness and robustness of the
Planning Committee.

Not recommended. This would fail to mitigate designation risk and
miss opportunities to improve decision quality and public
confidence.

PAS Recommendations (Preferred) Delivers measurable improvements to
committee operation, transparency, performance and community
engagement.

The Monitoring Authority for the Hinton

Monitoring Authority Role – the Monitoring

projects and enforcement where management is not carried out to the
agreed schedule. In being a signatory to the Inter-Authority
Agreement, all authorities agree to undertake the Monitoring
Authority role when requested. In respect of the Hinton Ampner
scheme, the Monitoring Authority will be required to spend around
half a day per year to review the monitoring report supplied by
Fareham Borough Council (as Host Authority) against the Monitoring
Plan and if required visit the site, and approve the reports
content or challenge it to the Solent Mitigation Parternship as
Lead Authority. The Solent Mitigation Partnership will provide a
fund to the Monitoring Authority which covers the officers time and
expenses when undertaking the monitoring activities over the
required monitoring period.

 

2.                
A Benefiting Authority for Test and
Itchen Mitigation Schemes at:

 

·      
Land at Woodington, Test
Valley

·      
Solent Householder Septic Tank Upgrade
Programme – Phase 1 (Arle Water Body, Bishops
Sutton)

·      
Basingstoke and Deane Borough Council
– Council-owned Sewage Works Upgrade, and

·      
Hinton Ampner Scheme, River
Itchen

 

Enabling the Council to secure nutrient
neutrality credits to support plan-making within East Hampshire
affected by both nitrogen and phosphorus in the Itchen catchment;
and to enter into the necessary legal and administrative
arrangements required to fulfil these roles, subject to compliance
with the Council’s constitutional, financial, and legal

content:
To receive and consider the recommendations in relation to

It was RESOLVED that the Shareholders Sub
Committee:
 

a.    
Approved, with
retrospective effect from June 2024, the introduction of two
temporary waste collection rounds by East Hampshire Norse Ltd, as
agreed in principle by the Shareholder Board in May 2024, thereby
completing the governance record for that change.

 

b.   
Approved the
continuation of the two additional temporary collection rounds
through 2025/26 and 2026/27, on the terms set out in this report,
to maintain service continuity while rerouting is completed and the
temporary rounds are stood down.

 
Reasons for the Decision
 

·      
Retrospective authorisation to
introduce two temporary core waste collection rounds from June
2024. This was agreed at the Shareholder Board (SHB) in May 2024
but was not subsequently brought to the Shareholders’
Subcommittee for sign-off as required by the governance framework;
and 
 

·      
Shareholder approval to continue those two additional temporary
core waste collection rounds in 2025/26 and 2026/27.

 
 
The Overview and Scrutiny Committee considered this item at
its meeting held on Thursday 2 April 2026 and made an additional
recommendation for the Shareholders Sub Committee to
consider:
 
“EHN and the Shareholder
Sub-Committee should agree a series of performance controls and/or
gates which are designed to show satisfactory progress of EHN in
their route re-routing. EHN will need to demonstrate performance
against these controls in the route re-routing every quarter to the
Shareholder Sub-committee. Should EHN want to access budget for
temporary rounds past September, they must demonstrate to the
Shareholder Sub-committee in September 2026 that these controls
have been fulfilled in order to access budget. After September,
budget will be approved in three monthly blocks - the first block
being October to December and the second block January to March.
Therefore EHN must return to the shareholder sub-committee in
December and demonstrate sufficient progress against controls to
access budget from January to March 2027.”
 
The Leader took the opportunity to thank the Overview and
Scrutiny Committee for their careful consideration of this item.
 
 
The Shareholders Sub Committee agreed not to take the
Overview and Scrutiny Committee recommendation forward, and
provided the following reasons that:
 
Having considered the recommendation
alongside the controls approved at this meeting, the Shareholders
Sub Committee was satisfied that the objective of the Overview and
Scrutiny Committee was to seek what already is secured within the
existing framework.
 
The Shareholders Sub-Committee had
approved that the monthly operational budget returns from EHN at
every SSC meeting, which is more frequent than the quarterly
cadence proposed. The full Reserved Matters regime had been
activated, meaning EHN cannot make any material commitment without
prior shareholder consent. The required revised Business Plan was
due by 30 June 2026, to set out a fully resolved position on the
temporary rounds before it can be approved.
 
Together these controls provide
equivalent, and in some respects stronger oversight than the
performance gate mechanism proposed.
 
The Chairman of the Overview and Scrutiny Committee would
be notified in relation to the decision taken by the Shareholders
Sub Committee. The Leader stated that he was fully committed in
keeping the Overview and Scrutiny Committee Chairman aware of any
future progress, through their regular reporting cycle.

purpose:
To receive and consider the recommendations in relation to
the report.
content:
To receive and consider the recommendations in relation to
the report.

It was RESOLVED that Shareholders Sub
Committee:
 
2.1     Approve the contract
extension
 

         
Approved the five-year contract extension between EHDC and EHN for
the period 29 March 2026 to 31 March 2031 on current commercial
terms, as to be approved by Cabinet at its meeting on 9 April 2026
noting:
 
(a)   
the rolling
18-month notice period exercisable by EHDC from 31 October 2026;
and
 
(b)   
the mutual option
to extend for a further five years by agreement.
 
2.2     REJECT the Business Plan
2026/27
 
Reject the EHN Business Plan for 2026/27
(Version 10, 3 March 2026) and its supporting appendices in their
current form on the grounds that:
(a)  The financial
baseline from which the Business Plan is constructed is
unresolved.  The Business Plan may not
cover the full core cost of delivering the service and cannot be
approved on that basis.
(b)  The Business
Plan does not fully comply with the requirements of clause 13.3 of
the Service Agreement. Business continuity planning is wholly
absent (clause 13.3.8); capital and resourcing schedules are
explicitly deferred (clauses 13.3.3 and 13.3.6); commercial income
is not disaggregated from core service income in the financial
model (clauses 13.3.9 and 13.3.10); and the explicit link to the
Council’s single integrated plan is absent (clause
13.3.2).
 
2.3     APPROVE interim operating
controls
 
In consequence of the rejection of the
Business Plan, and to allow EHN to continue to deliver services
lawfully during the period in which the Business Plan deficiencies
are addressed, resolve that the following interim controls shall
apply with immediate effect:
 
(a)   
EHN’s Annual
Charge for 2026/27 shall be paid at the prior year deemed rate in
accordance with Schedule 2 Part 3 paragraph 1.5 of the Service
Agreement, pending formal agreement of the Annual Charge through an
approved Business Plan. Officers will agree the precise monthly
payment figure with EHN and the Section 151 Officer and confirm
this to SSC in writing within 10 Business Days.
(b)   
The EHN Board of
Directors shall present monthly operational budget returns to SSC
at each SSC meeting during the interim period. Each return shall
set out income and expenditure against the prior year budget
baseline, identify any variance, and confirm that EHN is operating
within its current authority. Monthly SSC meetings shall be
convened for this purpose if not already scheduled.
(c)In the absence of an approved Business Plan,
all Reserved Matters under Schedule 1 of the Shareholders’
Agreement require the prior written consent of both shareholders
before EHN can act. This includes any expenditure or contractual
commitment that would otherwise have been authorised by an approved
Business Plan. The EHN Board is on notice that no Reserved Matter
may be proceeded with until shareholder consent is
obtained.
(d)  No new
permanent posts shall be created and no existing service
arrangements shall be terminated without prior written confirmation
from the Corporate Contracts and Partnerships Manager that
the  proposed action does not require
shareholder approval under clause 44.2 of the Service Agreement or
Schedule 1 of the Shareholders’ Agreement. The on-site fitter
proposal (Appendix 4 to the Business Plan) is specifically paused
pending this confirmation.
(e)  EHN shall
provide EHDC with open-book access to its profit and loss ledger in
accordance with clause 23.1(g) of the Shareholders’
Agreement. Any access issue shall be notified in writing and
resolved by EHN within 5 Business Days.
 
2.4     REQUIRE a revised Business
Plan
 
Require EHN to submit a revised Business
Plan to SSC no later than 30th  June
2026 The revised Business Plan must:
 
(a)  be founded on a
formally agreed and reconciled 2025/26 final outturn position,
including full resolution of the variations and the temporary
rounds funding mechanism;
(b)  set out a
resolved position on the two additional temporary rounds, including
whether they are to be retained or removed, the funding mechanism
for any that are retained, and the change control basis for that
decision;
(c)  set out a
resolved position on the overhead and management charge structure,
consistent with the scenarios modelled in Appendix 1 of the current
submission;
(d)  address all
outstanding clause 13.3 compliance gaps, including business
continuity planning, complete capital and resourcing schedules,
disaggregation of commercial income, and the link to the
Council’s single integrated plan; and
(e)  be submitted to
SSC in sufficient time to allow SSC to consider it at a properly
convened meeting before any financial commitment contingent on the
revised Business Plan is made.
 
2.5     DELEGATE authority
 
Delegate authority to the Corporate
Contracts and Partnerships Manager, in consultation with the
Section 151 Officer and Monitoring Officer, to:
 
(a)  agree and
confirm the monthly payment figure to EHN under the interim payment
arrangement at recommendation 2.3(a);
(b)  confirm in
writing to EHN the governance position on the on-site fitter
proposal and any other operational proposals brought forward during
the interim period; and
(c)  take all steps
necessary to progress formalisation of the contract extension
documentation with Trowers and Hamlins
LLP.
 
 
Reasons for the Decision
 
The reasons were set out at sections 4 and 5 of the report,
under the headings Business Plan 2026/27: Clause 13.3 Compliance
Assessment and Financial Concerns.
 
Alternative Options Considered
 
In the Officers’ assessment, they
were satisfied that endorsing the contract extension and rejection
of the Business Plan was the most compliant path available to the
Council and that the interim controls were temporary.
topline: The Shareholders Sub-Committee has decided to approve a contract extension but reject the Business Plan for 2026/27 due to financial concerns and non-compliance.

It was RESOLVED that Cabinet
NOTED:
 

·      
The outcome of the
Corporate Peer Challenge Review and the subsequent independent
report.

 

·      
The formal process
of Corporate Peer Challenge is now complete.

 
Reasons for the decision
 
The report was submitted to the Cabinet for information and
to note the outcome of the Progress Review, which took place in
January 2026. This review is an integral part the Corporate Peer
Challenge process. The review also allowed space and time for
progress on the original CPC Recommendations and to consider
peers’ reflections on the  opportunities and challenges that have arisen since
their original visit.  It also provided
a welcomed opportunity to demonstrate the impact and learning and
progress since the original review. 
 
Alternative Options Considered
 
To do nothing – this option is not recommended as
this would prevent the Council from learning from its peers from
the wider local government sector and would not demonstrate a
commitment to continuous improvement. To not review progress would
be contrary to the previous Cabinet decision and the requirements
of the CPC, whilst the formal review has concluded the council will
continue to learn and transform in line
with the changing situations.
 
*AS THIS ITEM WAS FOR NOTING, IT IS NOT
ELIGIBLE FOR CALL-IN*

additional funding of £376,000 has been met through
reallocation of existing East Hampshire District Council funds held
by the company.

 

b.   
Approved the continuation of the two temporary rounds in
2025/26. Noted that the £376,000 funding for this year has
yet to be confirmed and may be met through reallocation of existing
East Hampshire District Council funds held by the company, with any
shortfall (if required) will be provided from the Environmental
Service Reserve.

 

c.    
Approved the continuation of the two rounds for the year 2026/27
and agree additional contingent funding of £376,000 as a
variation to the waste collection contract. Note that the funding
(if required) will be provided from the Environmental Service
Reserve.

 

d.   
 Noted that the temporary rounds may
be removed before the end of 2026/27, subject to the rounds
restructuring programme.
 
 
Reasons for the decision
 
·      
For retrospective
permission to commission additional services from East Hampshire
Norse Ltd.
 

·      
To seek to
retrospectively regularise service and cost changes to the waste
collection service implemented to resolve significant service
issues that arose in 2024. They remain operationally necessary
until the rerouting work is completed, absorbing the additional
workload into the permanent round structure.

 
Alternative Options Considered
 
Officers considered three options:
 
Option 1:
Approve budget allocation for temporary rounds
in 25/26 and 26/27 (RECOMMENDED)
 
Option 2:
Decline budget allocation; If sufficient
in-year efficiencies are not found for 25/26 , EHN would need to
seek shareholder investment to fund the budget shortfall and
immediately terminate the additional servies.to absorb cost or
stand down rounds immediately.
 
Option 3:
Approve partial budget allocation (e.g. 1 year
only).
 
Officers recommended Option 1 as the only
viable approach that maintains service continuity and allows the
restructuring work to be completed without operational
pressure.

extension then followed by another 1 year optional extension making
a maximum total of four years, after which the contract is
reviewed.  

It was RESOLVED that the Cabinet
approved:
 
 

a.    
The procurement of
an external provider via an open tender process, with a 2 + 1 + 1
structure and the ability for either party to terminate after year
2 subject to the agreed terms and conditions.
 

b.   
Authorisation to
enter into the successful contract be delegated to the Executive
Director of Operations and that the allocation of S106 funding for
the cost of the contract (see Appendix 1 Exempt) be delegated to
the Whitehill & Bordon Portfolio Holder and the Executive
Director of Operations in consultation with the Council’s
Monitoring Officer and S151 Officer.

 

c.    
Delegate authority
to the Principal Policy Planner to finalise the specification, use
the tender, evaluate the bids in accordance with the stated
methodology, and award the contract to the chosen
tenderer.

 

d.   
Note that the
contract will be funded from the ring-fenced Section 106 developer
contributions collected to deliver the SAMM in perpetuity for
Whitehill & Bordon, with no additional General Fund budget
required.

 
Reasons for the decision
 
To seek approval to procure and award a 4-year
contract with a 2 + 1 + 1 structure (1 June 2026 – 31 May
2030) for the continued delivery of the Whitehill & Bordon
Strategic Access Management and Monitoring (SAMM) measures for the
Wealden Heaths Phase II Special Protection Area (SPA), Woolmer
Forest and Shortheath Common Special
Areas of Conservation (SAC) which is funded by existing developer
contributions.
 
Alternative Options
Considered
 
Option 1 Do
Nothing
 
If the council did not procure a new SAMM
provider and let the service lapse after March 2026, the council
would fail its legal duties under the Habitats Regulations and
existing planning obligation agreements (because SAMM is required
mitigation for new development as part of the Whitehill &
Bordon strategic allocation); this would expose the council to
legal challenge,
reputational damage and environmental harm.
This is not a viable option and carries a high legal and
environmental risk.
 
Option 2
 
In-House (staff to provide the service.) The
council would recruit staff to act as rangers, ecological monitors,
engagement officers and project managers. The service requires
specialist ecological expertise, equipment and capacity the council
does not have. It would likely require significant new staffing and
training costs. The project covers multiple landholdings and
specialist surveys which require external accredited ecologists.
This option would be costly, high-risk and resource-intensive and
does not represent best value.
 
Option 3
 
Procure an External Provider (Recommended
Option) Provides the specialist skills and capacity needed for
ecological monitoring, seasonal ranger work, engagement and site
management. Ensures continuous legal compliance with the Habitats
Regulations and existing planning obligations agreements, and is
fully funded by those existing ring-fenced Section 106
contributions. This is the lowest risk, most cost-effective and
legally robust option.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to appoint an external service provider for a 4-year contract to carry out legal duties under the Habitats Regulations for the Wealden Heath Phase II Special Protection Area.

To consider the proposal for Citizens Advice
Core Funding for 2026/27.

RESOLVED that
 
a.

to Citizens Advice East Hampshire at £186,000 per annum for
the delivery of advice services in East Hampshire be
approved;
b.   
the continuation of funding under a three-year
Service Level Agreement commencing 1 April 2026 and ending 31 March
2029, subject to annual review as part of the Council’s
budget-setting process be approved; and
c.   
authority be delegated to the Executive Director
of Community, in consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Community Development and Engagement and the Section 151 Officer,
to:

•      
Finalise and enter into the contractual
arrangements with Citizens Advice East Hampshire;

•      
Agree detailed outcomes, monitoring arrangements,
and any variations required during the term of the agreement;
and

•      
Release grant payments in instalments subject to
satisfactory performance monitoring.
 
Reasons for the decision
 
To enter into a new funding agreement with
Citizens Advice East Hampshire (CAEH) for the continued delivery of
free, confidential, and impartial advice services to residents
across East Hampshire. The proposal was to move from the current
one-year arrangement to a three-year Service Level Agreement (SLA),
with an annual review clause linked to the Council’s budget
setting process.
 
Alternative Options Considered
 
Option A – Do Nothing
No statutory duty exists to fund advice
services. However, withdrawal of funding would likely result in
service closure, increased demand on statutory services, and
negative impacts on vulnerable residents.
 
Option B – One-Year Extension
Maintains current arrangements but offers
limited security for CAEH and does not address long-term
sustainability. Risk of service reduction remains high.
 
Option C – Three-Year SLA with Annual
Review (Preferred)
Provides greater operational stability for
CAEH, reducing the risk of service reduction by enabling
longer-term planning and more favourable supplier contracts Page 5
of 9 (e.g. telephony and advice systems). Supports continuity
during LGR while retaining annual financial control and break
clauses for the Council.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to renew core funding for Citizens Advice East Hampshire for the delivery of advice services in East Hampshire.

purpose:
To consider the community services grant awards for
2026/27
content:
To consider the community services grant awards for
2026/27

RESOLVED that
 

1.   
the continuation of core services grant funding
for Community First East Hampshire, Community Transport Services
and the Hampshire Safeguarding Children Partnership, as set out in
Section 7, up to a maximum total value of £95,200 for 2026/27
be approved; and

2.   
authority be delegated to the Executive Director
of Community, in consultation with the Portfolio Holder for
Community Development and Engagement and the Section 151 Officer,
to:
·      
agree and enter into the necessary grant and
service level agreements;
·      
agree performance monitoring and break
clauses;
·      
release grant payments in instalments subject to
performance; and
·      
where funding and budgets allow, extend or vary
the term of agreements beyond one year, up to the approved
budget.
 
Reasons for the decision
 
To continue existing core services funding
arrangements for key community services operating in East Hampshire
for the period April 2026 to March 2027 (and beyond where delegated
authority is exercised), within the approved Community Services
revenue budget.
 
Alternative Options Considered
 
A. Do nothing
There is no statutory requirement for the
Council to provide funding for these services. However, this option
would have significant negative consequences. Community First plays
a critical role in supporting the voluntary sector, which underpins
the Council’s ambitions for thriving communities and an
asset-based approach. Without this support, many local
organisations would struggle to remain viable, reducing community
capacity and resilience. Similarly, the withdrawal of funding for
Community Transport would exacerbate rural isolation and limit
access to essential services, particularly for older residents and
those with mobility challenges. This would likely increase demand
on statutory services and lead to poorer health and wellbeing
outcomes.
 
B. Council provides services directly
The Council could seek to deliver these
services in-house. However, this is not considered feasible or
cost-effective. The Council does not have the specialist expertise
or staff resources to replicate the infrastructure support provided
by Community First or the operational capacity to deliver community
transport. Partner organisations can leverage external funding,
volunteer support, and economies of scale to deliver these services
more efficiently than the Council could achieve alone.
 
C. Reduce the current level of grant
funding
Reducing the level of funding would compromise
the ability of Community First to maintain a dedicated officer for
East Hampshire and deliver the full range of support services
required to build capacity in the voluntary sector. This would
undermine the Council’s strategic objectives, including the
development of Community Area Partnerships and the implementation
of ABCD principles. Similarly, reducing funding for Community
Transport would result in fewer routes or reduced service
availability, leaving vulnerable residents without viable transport
options. While both services attract some external funding, these
sources are typically short-term and cannot replace core
funding.
 
D. Preferred option - Maintain funding as
proposed
The recommended approach is to maintain the
current level of funding for Community First and Community
Transport, as set out in this report. This option ensures
continuity of essential services while supporting the
Council’s transformation agenda. It also provides flexibility
for Community Transport through delegated authority to agree annual
contractual arrangements, enabling the Council to respond to budget
pressures and service changes over the three-year period.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the continuation of core services grant funding for key community services in East Hampshire for the period of 2026/27.

purpose:
To receive and consider the report in relation to a policy
decision to offer a reward to members of the public for recognition
of their time and effort to support enforcement action against fly
tipping.
content:
To receive and consider the report in relation to a policy
decision to offer a reward to members of the public for recognition
of their time and effort to support enforcement action against fly
tipping.

RESOLVED that

1.   
The introduction of a witness reward scheme,
based on the following criteria, be approved:
a.   
An offence being actually witnessed by a member
of the public. Physical evidence alone e.g. items found at the
scene would not qualify for a reward.
b.   
Rewards would only be considered if the
information provided leads to a formal enforcement result such
as:

• A Fixed Penalty Notice being paid in full by
the offender
• A
successful criminal prosecution (with or without the witness
attending)
The reward
is to provide recompense for individuals for the time they spend
assisting the authority in successful action.

2.   
authority be delegated to the Executive Director
to approve the final scheme/policy, including any relevant updates
from time to time.
 
Reasons for the decision
 
Fly tipping continues to be an issue for local
authorities in England and Wales, and some councils have adopted a
witness reward scheme to support with their investigations and act
as a deterrent. This seeks to enhance the likelihood of a witness
coming forward and offering information that could lead to a
conviction. Members of the public who fulfil their public duty and
sacrifice time, provide information, give witness statements,
attend court etc are vital to successful enforcement.
 
Alternative Options Considered
 

1.   
Do nothing – continue with current
investigation techniques without a reward scheme to encourage
witnesses to come forward.

2.   
Implement a reward scheme – add a witness
reward scheme to our toolkit with a view to improving the chances
of a successful prosecution or penalty notice being served, in the
event of a fly-tip taking place in our district.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to introduce a witness reward scheme to encourage public support in enforcement action against fly tipping.

purpose:
Cabinet to consider recommendations to Council, in respect
of the ARC Programmen.
content:
Cabinet to consider recommendations to Council, in respect
of the ARC Programmen.

It was RESOLVED that Cabinet:
 
o  
Agreed the revised
objectives of the Programme set out in Section 5.1

 
o  
Approved the
proposed re-branding of transformation activity under the banner of
the ‘ARC’ (Adapt, Reskill, Collaborate) and subsequent
launch of an internal communications plan set out in Section
5.1.
 
o  
Agreed the
inclusion of Devolution, Local Government Reorganisation and the
New Unitary and Combined Authority Leader in the revised list of
‘ARC’ transformation initiatives summarised in Section
5.

 
o  
Noted the
indicative costs of the revised transformation activity, summarised
in Section 6

 
Reasons for the Decision
 
This paper was submitted to Cabinet to update
Members and to seek approval to move forward with additional
transformation initiatives since those approved in September 2024.
This has been made necessary by the reorganisation of local government in Hampshire and
the Isle of Wight; together with devolution which includes the
creation of a new unitary authority and Mayoral Combined County
Authority. This has led to a necessary reshaping and re-focusing of
transformation initiatives and a refreshed programme branding - now called the ARC
Programme (Adapt, Reskill,
Collaborate)
 
Alternative Options
Considered
 
In 2021 East Hampshire District Council (EHDC)
embarked on an ambitious transformation programme called Shaping East Hampshire’s
Future which includes the delivery of the 2024-28 Council Strategy,
in particular the strategic objective to become a modern and
efficient council.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve additional transformation initiatives under the ARC Programme in response to local government reorganisation and devolution in Hampshire and the Isle of Wight.

To request to Cabinet the adoption of an updated version of
the Council’s Statement of Community Involvement (SCI), to be
referred to as “SCI 2025”.
 
Alternative Options Considered

Do nothing – maintain the Statement of Community
Involvement
2024, which was not recommended by officers on the basis

Preferred option – to adopt the Statement of
Community Involvement 2025 was the only option that enables the
Council to meet its statutory obligations of the Planning and
Compulsory Purchase Act 2004 to support the communities engagement
with planning matters via varying methods of
consultation.

purpose:

content:
For the Cabinet to consider the recommendations in relation
to the designation of Horndean Parish
as a neighbourhood area.

It was RESOLVED that the
Cabinet:
 
Approved the Horndean Parish Council application for the parish
to be a designated neighbourhood area.
 
Reasons for the Decision

For the determination of the application submitted by
Horndean Parish Council to East
Hampshire District Council (EHDC), for the designation of the
parish as a neighbourhood area.
 
Alternative Options Considered
 
Option 1
Do nothing and do not approve the designation
of Horndean Parish to be a neighbourhood area This option is not recommended
by Officers on the basis that it would not be legally compliant
with Section 61G of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
 
Option 2
 
Approve the designation for Horndean Parish to be a neighbourhood area. As the
submission from the Parish Council is in accordance with the
Neighbourhood Planning (General) Regulations 2012 Regulation 5, it
is desirable for the entire parish to be designated and the
designation would not impact any other existing designated
boundaries, there is no reason not to approve the
designation.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the designation of Horndean Parish as a neighbourhood area.

content:
RESOLVED that it was:
 
Approved to provide the shareholder
consent for East Hampshire Norse Ltd to enter into a Limitation of
Liability Agreement with PricewaterhouseCoopers for the statutory
audit of the 2024/25 financial accounts.
 
Reasons for the
decision
 
To provide decision on a limitation of liability agreement
(LLA) with the company's auditors is a matter reserved for the
shareholders under Schedule 1, Part 1, Section EE of the
Shareholders' Agreement. (Appendix 1)
 
As per the Council's updated constitution, the Shareholder
Sub Committee has the delegated authority from Cabinet to exercise
shareholder consents directly. A formal decision was sought from
the Sub Committee to approve the company’s request to enter
an LLA for the 2024/25 statutory audit.
 
Alternative Options
Considered
 
Officers reviewed the proposal and considered the risk to
the Council to be low. Refusing to enter into the LLA would prevent
the finalisation of the company’s statutory accounts,
representing a significant compliance failure. Given the
Shareholders Sub Committee's delegated authority, a direct decision
can now be made.
topline: The Shareholders Sub-Committee has decided to approve providing shareholder consent for East Hampshire Norse Ltd to enter into a Limitation of Liability Agreement with PricewaterhouseCoopers for the statutory audit of the 2024/25 financial accounts.
